title: Ink-Wash Studio
premise: A long master-apprentice drama of Listening Rain studio and the bamboo-corridor brush-washing pool. Ayue and Amo look nearly alike and are easily mistaken; the goat-hair doubi brush goes intact→tip splayed→tip rewrapped; the pine-soot inkstone boat shatters and must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_brushman: Ink-wash painter Wu Yue around fifty, lean long face, washed moon-white long robe with pale ink on the cuffs, right hand forever gripping goat hair, quiet look.
states.frail_leaning: The same Wu Yue: pale face, moon-white robe hanging loose, must lean on the painting-table edge to walk slowly, knuckles trembling from long illness.
states.deceased: Wu Yue has closed his eyes and passed away, lying quietly on a bamboo couch in the studio, face peaceful, no breath left.

states.young_apprentice: Young Ayue: a lean studio apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, a bamboo-green hairpin in the hair, light-gray short jacket, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Adult Ayue: a young painter in the twenties with an easy upright back, still the bamboo-green hairpin, short jacket swapped for a moon-white cover shirt, steady eyes.

states.intact: An oversized goat-hair doubi brush, bamboo shaft carved with the words Listening Rain, tip neat and full, root wrapped in cream silk thread.
states.tip_splayed: The same goat-hair doubi brush with tip splayed and stiffened, ink seeping from a crack in the bamboo shaft, silk thread loose and soaked with overnight ink.
states.tip_rewrapped: After tip repair the goat-hair doubi brush tip gathers again; the bamboo crack is filled with raw lacquer; the silk thread is rewound tight.

states.intact: A thread-bound teaching painting manual with a deep-cyan cover, pages demonstrating texture strokes and washes, paper white and writing clear.
states.ink_soaked: The same teaching painting manual soaked through by spilled inkstone ink, cover wrinkled, demonstration drawings blurred into a blot.

states.intact: An elm inkstone boat: a boat-shaped stone set with a Duan inkstone, pine-soot ink stick and water pot beside it, wave patterns carved on the gunwales.
states.shattered_overturned: The elm inkstone boat has fallen from the painting table and shattered; the Duan inkstone broken in two, ink spilled across the floor.

states.young_rival: Young painter Amo whose face closely resembles Ayue's, but a vermilion silk cord around the wrist, black short jacket over, flamboyant look.
states.remade_face: After remaking his look, Amo still wears the vermilion silk cord on the wrist; black short jacket swapped for crow-blue, expression deeper.

E7.name: Listening Rain studio
E7.appearance: Waterside Listening Rain studio, north window pasted with white xuan, a wide elm painting table at center, undried landscape scrolls on the wall, air rich with ink scent.

E8.name: bamboo-corridor brush-washing pool
E8.appearance: The bamboo corridor outside the studio; a bluestone brush-washing pool holds pale-gray ink water; bamboo shadows fall sparsely on the stone rim.

E9.name: xuan-paper storeroom alley
E9.appearance: A narrow alley between xuan-paper storerooms, paper racks towering on both sides, damp-proof bamboo mats on the floor, light chopped by paper rolls.

E10.name: old gallery ruin hall
E10.appearance: The south-city old gallery ruin hall; peeling white walls still show hanging-nail marks; empty scroll shafts and torn silk piled in a corner.

E11.name: studio memorial wood plaque
E11.appearance: A nanmu plaque nailed to the studio doorpost, carved with Wu Yue and the founding year, corners polished bright by touch.

E12.name: mineral-color saucers
E12.appearance: Three blue-white porcelain mineral-color saucers holding azurite, malachite, and vermilion respectively, set at the upper-right of the painting table.

E13.name: rosewood seal-box cart
E13.appearance: A small cart pushing a rosewood seal box, body lacquered black, brass corners bright—utterly unlike the elm inkstone boat.

E14.name: academy steward
E14.appearance: A lean academy steward in a deep-brown skullcap and blue-gray long robe, build somewhat like Wu Yue's, but a jade waist plaque on the chest.

E15.name: tung-oil shade lamps
E15.appearance: A row of five tung-oil shade lamps hung on iron hooks under the studio beams, shades polished clear.

E16.name: apprentice-calling bronze qing
E16.appearance: Two apprentice-calling bronze qing hung under the bamboo-corridor eaves, strike marks on the rims, tapped twice before class.

E17.name: Xiaodi
E17.appearance: New mounting apprentice Xiaodi in a light-brown hairband and brand-new short jacket; at a glance like young Ayue, but a sharper chin and shy unfamiliar eyes.

E18.name: weasel-hair small-kai brush
E18.appearance: A weasel-hair small-kai brush somewhat like a doubi but much shorter; black-lacquer shaft, no Listening Rain carving.

E19.name: rosewood brush rest
E19.appearance: A rosewood brush rest with scrolling-cloud carving on the bed, able to hold several brushes—not the same as a boat-shaped inkstone.

segments.action: At dusk, Wu Yue lifts the moon-white long-robe sleeve and enters Listening Rain studio, dips the goat-hair doubi brush in ink to test the tip.
A row of five tung-oil shade lamps hangs under the studio beams; Wu Yue polishes each shade.
Two apprentice-calling bronze qing hang under the bamboo-corridor eaves; Wu Yue taps lightly; the tone rings clear.
Wu Yue checks the goat-hair doubi brush tip and silk wrapping, confirming no splay.
Through the north window, Wu Yue looks at ink-colored reflections wrinkled by wind on the pool.
The intact goat-hair doubi brush rests on the brush mountain; the tip catches warm tung-oil light.
Wu Yue sits by the painting table and drinks a sip of warm tea.
Distant boat sounds rise; he spreads half-sized raw xuan again.
He first outlines distant mountains in pale ink, lines like floating silk.
Night deepens; he hangs the undried scroll at a draft to dry.
Wu Yue opens the thread-bound teaching painting manual and notes today's texture-stroke points with weasel hair on a blank page.
At a corner of the manual he sketches an axe-cut texture stroke.
Wu Yue closes the teaching painting manual and tucks it into the lower drawer of the painting table.
Ink rhyme from the goat-hair doubi brush on paper sweeps his profile.
He tears a scrap of waste xuan and wipes overnight ink from the inkstone edge.
By the morning bamboo-corridor brush-washing pool, Wu Yue greets the figure hurrying in with the pine-soot inkstone boat.
Young Ayue sets the pine-soot inkstone boat steadily on the bluestone rim; the bamboo-green hairpin sways lightly.
Wu Yue points to the three mineral-color saucers at the upper-right of the painting table and teaches Ayue to tell azurite from malachite.
Ayue crouches by the brush-washing pool, curiously stirring a pool of pale ink water.
Wu Yue explains to Ayue that when the bronze qing sounds twice, the brush must stop and the tip be gathered.
Ayue glances back at the intact pine-soot inkstone boat, eyes full of longing.
Bamboo shadows sway; the two walk back along the bamboo corridor to Listening Rain studio.
In the xuan-paper storeroom alley, Amo with a vermilion silk cord on the wrist turns from behind a paper-rack shadow.

segments.action: In the spring-rain season, Wu Yue day after day outlines, textures, and washes in the studio.
Another rainy night, he pulls the moon-white long robe tight and keeps watch by the goat-hair doubi brush.
At high summer noon, xuan softens with damp; he rotates sheets to dry.
Autumn mist fills the air; tung-oil light struggles through the ink scent.
On New Year's Eve, Wu Yue alone fills teaching notes to the last page.
In early spring he regrinds pine soot and continues teaching demonstrations.
Before plum-rain season, Wu Yue reinforces the storeroom damp-proof mats.
After Frost's Descent he adds a small charcoal basin in a studio corner.
Another year before a gathering, he checks each scroll for exhibit.
On a snowy night he stops the brush, leaves only one tung-oil shade lamp, and keeps watch until dawn.
After Jingzhe he rebound the loose attachment pages of the teaching painting manual.
Wu Yue changes the brush curtain and hangs washed brushes to air-dry.
He checks the brush-washing pool water level and scoops out ink that is too thick.
He lifts the intact goat-hair doubi brush again and tests the tip once in pale ink.
Paper-pounding rhythm comes from outside the corridor; he looks up to listen.
Wu Yue pours waste ink into a pottery jar and covers it.
At noon rest he drinks tea under the bamboo corridor; tea smoke coils past bamboo green.
In the afternoon he returns to the painting table and continues texturing a stretch of distant mountain.
At sunset he covers the inkstone pool and locks the studio door.
Before night he patrols the paper storeroom once more to confirm no rats.
At dawn, Wu Yue patrols along the bamboo-corridor brush-washing pool; the pine-soot inkstone boat still rests on the stone rim.
He crouches to check whether the wave-pattern carving on the pine-soot inkstone boat gunwales is intact.
At the upper-right of the painting table, those earlier three mineral-color saucers still sit in place.
A rosewood brush rest is carried past the bamboo corridor—scrolling-cloud bed, not the pine-soot inkstone boat.
Standing in the bamboo corridor, Wu Yue logs ripples last night's damp left on the xuan.
He resets the inkstone boat and presses a sheet of blotting paper on it.
Distant market sounds rise; morning mist begins to clear.
At nightfall, Wu Yue returns to Listening Rain studio and opens the ink-soaked teaching painting manual.

segments.action: A rosewood seal-box cart is pushed past the bamboo corridor—nothing like the shattered pine-soot inkstone boat.
An academy steward in a skullcap walks into the bamboo corridor and talks beside Wu Yue; the two builds are alike.
The steward points at the rosewood seal-box cart to explain the seal-borrowing plan.
The cart leaves; Wu Yue alone watches it go from the brush-washing pool.
He resets the mineral-color saucers and walks back to the studio.
Into the xuan-paper storeroom alley comes mounting apprentice Xiaodi in a light-brown hairband; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Ayue.
Xiaodi practices rolling xuan; Wu Yue shakes his head—she is not Ayue after all.
Xiaodi bows her head and steps back; only paper-rack shadows remain in the alley.
Years later at dusk, pale Wu Yue, as if leaning on a painting table, stands under the old gallery ruin hall.
